title: How to Choose and Cast a Voice Over Artist
h1: How to choose and cast a voice over artist
description: Choose a voice over artist: define the voice, collect samples, run a short audition, compare readers, agree rights and prepare scripts and direction.
intro: The right voice makes a video, ad, course or audiobook feel professional, and the wrong one can undermine it. Choosing a voice is partly taste, but a clear process helps you decide with confidence. This article explains how to describe the voice you need, how to listen to samples, how to run a fair audition and what to agree before the recording.

faq.q: How do I describe the voice I want?
faq.a: Use a few words for tone, age range, energy and accent, and share examples of voices you like.

faq.q: Should I ask for an audition?
faq.a: A short test read of a few lines from your script is common and helps compare voices fairly. Ask whether it is free or paid.
Say where the recording will be used, for how long and in which regions. Ask for the license in writing.
Mark emphasis, pace and mood in the script, and give examples of how a line should sound.

faq.q: Can I change the script later?
faq.a: Small changes may be allowed. Larger changes usually count as new work, so finish the script first.
